function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for a local bakery, a specialty shop, or an online delivery service.

---

## 1. Local Bakeries & Specialty Shops  
These are great if you want a freshly baked, custom‑made cake and often offer in‑store pickup or local delivery.

| Platform | What to Look For | Tips |
|----------|------------------|------|
| **Local Bakery** | Check their website or Instagram for menu photos, custom options, and delivery radius. | Call ahead to confirm availability and delivery times. |
| **Specialty Cake Shops** | Look for shops that specialize in wedding cakes, birthday cakes, or themed desserts. | Ask about customization (flavors, designs, dietary restrictions). |
| **Farmers’ Markets** | Some vendors sell pre‑made cakes or offer custom orders. | Great for seasonal flavors and supporting local producers. |

---

## 2. Online Delivery Services (U.S. & Canada)

| Service | How It Works | Pros | Cons |
|---------|--------------|------|------|
| **Uber Eats** | Browse local restaurants & bakeries; place order via app. | Fast delivery, real‑time tracking. | Delivery fees + tip. |
| **DoorDash** | Similar to Uber Eats; includes “DashPass” subscription for free delivery on many orders. | Wide selection, frequent promos. | Delivery fee + tip. |
| **Postmates** | Offers “Postmates Unlimited” for free delivery on orders over $9.99. | Good for last‑minute orders. | Delivery fee + tip. |
| **Instacart** | Order from grocery stores (e.g., Whole Foods, Safeway) that carry cakes. | Grocery pickup & delivery. | Delivery fee + tip. |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Fresh food delivery, including cakes from local vendors. | Convenient, fast delivery. | Delivery fee + tip. |
| **Grubhub** | Large network of restaurants & bakeries. | Frequent discounts. | Delivery fee + tip. |

> **Tip:** Many of these apps let you filter by “Bakery” or “Dessert” and show ratings/reviews. Look for “Custom Orders” or “Special Requests” options.

---

## 3. Specialty Cake Delivery Sites

| Site | What They Offer | Why Use Them |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| **Etsy** | Handmade, custom cakes from independent bakers worldwide. | Unique designs, direct communication with the baker. |
| **Cake Delivery (UK)** | UK‑based cake delivery service. | Same‑day delivery in major cities. |
| **Baker’s Dozen (Australia)** | Australian bakery delivery. | Fresh, local ingredients. |
| **Local Bakery Websites** | Many local bakeries now have their own online ordering system. | Direct support for local businesses. |

---

## 4. Things to Consider When Ordering a Cake

| Factor | What to Check | How to Verify |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| **Flavor & Ingredients** | Ask about allergens, gluten‑free, vegan options. | Request a sample or ingredient list. |
| **Size & Portion** | Confirm the number of servings. | Ask for a portion estimate. |
| **Delivery Time** | Make sure the delivery window fits your event. | Confirm pickup/delivery time with the vendor. |
| **Price** | Compare prices across platforms. | Look for hidden fees (delivery, tip). |
| **Reviews** | Read recent customer feedback. | Check ratings on Google, Yelp, or the platform itself. |
| **Customization** | Discuss design, icing, decorations. | Send photos or sketches if possible. |

---

## 5. Quick Starter List (U.S. & Canada)

| City | Best Local Bakery | Best Online Option |
|------|-------------------|--------------------|
| New York | Levain Bakery | DoorDash |
| Los Angeles | Baked by Melissa | Uber Eats |
| Chicago | Magnolia Bakery | Grubhub |
| Toronto | Sweet Tooth Bakery | Instacart |
| Vancouver | The Sweet Spot | Uber Eats |
| London | The Cake Shop | Deliveroo (UK) |
| Sydney | Sweet & Sassy | Menulog (Australia) |

> *If you’re outside the U.S. or Canada, just replace the local bakery with a local specialty shop and use the nearest equivalent of Uber Eats/Grubhub.*

---

### Final Thought

If you have a specific city or region in mind, let me know and I can narrow down the best options for you. Happy cake hunting! 🍰
